title: Three weeks of Central Texas pulling back from Flock
subtitle: Dates are the days KXAN reported each step
alt: Timeline of Central Texas jurisdictions withdrawing from Flock license plate reader cameras in August 2026: Burnet County removing all of its cameras on Aug. 5, Lago Vista voting unanimously to remove its cameras on Aug. 8, Flock announcing new privacy guardrails on Aug. 13, Pflugerville delaying its renewal vote on Aug. 15, and Pflugerville switching its system off and declining a new contract on Aug. 25
source: KXAN, CBS Austin and FOX 7 Austin

events.label: Burnet County removes all of its Flock cameras
events.note: Sheriff Calvin Boyd cited public concerns; two had been vandalized

events.label: Lago Vista council votes unanimously to remove cameras
events.note: Followed a citizen petition drive over privacy and surveillance

events.label: Flock announces new privacy guardrails
events.note: Seven-day default retention, mandatory misuse detection, case codes

events.label: Pflugerville delays its vote on a $175,000 renewal
events.note: Mayor Doug Weiss cited concerns over data retention and sharing

events.label: Pflugerville switches the system off, declines the contract
events.note: Cameras covered after a resident's records request on data access
